#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Build OS — route-task.sh: issues a ROUTING RECEIPT, one file per routing
# decision, under build-os/packets/routing/ (or --out DIR).
#
# WHY THIS EXISTS. EXP-0002's sealed records carry the executed defect this
# tool closes half of: buildos T5 ran Full ceremony (4 subagent dispatches,
# $4.80, 7.4M total tokens) while its own run record read
# `mode_selector_says: gravito_light`. The verdict existed and bound nothing,
# because nothing durable recorded "this is what was selected, these are the
# budgets, and here is where the executed mode must be reconciled". The receipt
# is that record. build-os/tools/routing-check.sh is the close-time gate that
# refuses a receipt whose executed_mode exceeds its selected_mode with no
# escalation record. Contract: build-os/memory/routing_contract.md.
#
# THE BUDGETS ARE DERIVED DEFAULTS, NOT LAWS — operator-tunable, derived from
# EXP-0002's sealed run records and stated with their derivation:
#   * Light band: the ON surface's light runs measured 172,261/368,831/229,190
#     TOTAL tokens (buildos T1/T2/T4, 0 dispatches) — max 368,831, so the 500k
#     light default has headroom. NAMED EXCEEDANCE: raw-arm T4 measured 526,461
#     at 0 dispatches; the light budget governs the ON surface, whose measured
#     max is the basis; raw figures are context, not the band.
#   * The two blowouts measured 4.9M (T3) and 7.4M (T5) total tokens, 5 and 4
#     dispatches, $3.63 and $4.80, ~849s and ~1013s wall clock.
#   Full defaults sit between the two bands — generous against the light band,
#   a hard ceiling well under the blowouts:
#     max_subagents 3 (blowouts dispatched 4-5), max_total_tokens 2,000,000
#     (blowouts 4.9M/7.4M), max_uncached_tokens 120,000, max_model_calls 40,
#     max_wall_clock_s 900, max_cost_usd 1.50 (blowouts $3.63/$4.80).
#   Light defaults bound the measured light band with headroom (~370k max
#   observed -> 500k), and direct is half of light again. Every number here is
#   a DERIVED DEFAULT an operator may retune; none is a claim of optimality.
#
# Usage:
#   route-task.sh --task-id ID --description TEXT --descriptor JSON [--out DIR]
#
#   ID          [A-Za-z0-9._-]+ — becomes part of the receipt file name.
#   TEXT        free text; only its sha256 is recorded (the receipt must not
#               become a second copy of the task prompt).
#   JSON        the full 13-field descriptor mode-select.mjs requires.
#
# Output: the receipt path and the selected mode on stdout.
# Exit: 0 with a receipt written; 2 on malformed input, a selector refusal, or
# a pre-existing receipt file (one file per decision — never overwrite).
# Writes EXACTLY ONE file, in the caller-named directory, and nothing else.
set -uo pipefail

SELF_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO="$(cd "$SELF_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
MODE_SELECT="$SELF_DIR/mode-select.mjs"

refuse(){ printf 'route-task: REFUSED — %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit 2; }

TASK_ID=""; DESCRIPTION=""; DESCRIPTOR=""; OUT_DIR="$REPO/build-os/packets/routing"
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --task-id)     [ $# -ge 2 ] || refuse "--task-id needs a value";     TASK_ID="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --description) [ $# -ge 2 ] || refuse "--description needs a value"; DESCRIPTION="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --descriptor)  [ $# -ge 2 ] || refuse "--descriptor needs a value";  DESCRIPTOR="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --out)         [ $# -ge 2 ] || refuse "--out needs a value";         OUT_DIR="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    -h|--help)     sed -n '2,45p' "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}"; exit 0 ;;
    *) refuse "unknown option \"$1\"" ;;
  esac
done

[ -n "$TASK_ID" ]     || refuse "no --task-id. A receipt that identifies no task reconciles nothing."
case "$TASK_ID" in
  *[!A-Za-z0-9._-]*) refuse "task id \"$TASK_ID\" carries characters outside [A-Za-z0-9._-]. The id becomes a file name; a path-shaped id is a write outside the receipt store." ;;
esac
[ -n "$DESCRIPTION" ] || refuse "no --description. The description hash is what binds the receipt to the task that was actually routed."
[ -n "$DESCRIPTOR" ]  || refuse "no --descriptor. A routing decision without its descriptor is a verdict nobody can re-derive."
[ -f "$MODE_SELECT" ] || refuse "no selector at $MODE_SELECT"
command -v node >/dev/null 2>&1 || refuse "node is not available, and the selector is not re-implemented here — two implementations of one rule is how they diverge"

# The verdict comes from the ONE selector, never re-derived here. Its stderr
# (the withheld-Full note) is captured into the receipt: a downgrade that is
# printed once and scrolls away is a downgrade nobody audits.
NOTE_FILE="$(mktemp)"; trap 'rm -f "$NOTE_FILE"' EXIT
if ! SELECTED="$(node "$MODE_SELECT" "$DESCRIPTOR" 2>"$NOTE_FILE")"; then
  sed 's/^/route-task: /' "$NOTE_FILE" >&2
  refuse "the selector refused the descriptor (above). A receipt is never issued on a guessed mode."
fi
SELECTED="$(printf '%s' "$SELECTED" | tr -d '[:space:]')"
case "$SELECTED" in direct|gravito_light|gravito_full) ;; *) refuse "the selector returned \"$SELECTED\", which is not a mode this tool issues receipts for" ;; esac
SELECTOR_NOTE="$(tr '\n' ' ' < "$NOTE_FILE" | sed 's/[[:space:]]*$//')"
[ -n "$SELECTOR_NOTE" ] || SELECTOR_NOTE="-"

# Per-mode budgets — DERIVED DEFAULTS (derivation in the header), not laws.
case "$SELECTED" in
  gravito_full)
    B_SUB=3;  B_TOT=2000000; B_UNC=120000; B_CALLS=40; B_WALL=900; B_COST="1.50" ;;
  gravito_light)
    B_SUB=0;  B_TOT=500000;  B_UNC=60000;  B_CALLS=25; B_WALL=600; B_COST="0.75" ;;
  direct)
    B_SUB=0;  B_TOT=250000;  B_UNC=30000;  B_CALLS=12; B_WALL=300; B_COST="0.40" ;;
esac

DESC_SHA="$(printf '%s' "$DESCRIPTION" | sha256sum | awk '{print $1}')"
ISSUED_AT="$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"
STAMP="$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)"

mkdir -p -- "$OUT_DIR" 2>/dev/null || refuse "cannot create receipt directory $OUT_DIR"
RECEIPT="$OUT_DIR/routing-$TASK_ID-$STAMP.md"
[ -e "$RECEIPT" ] && refuse "a receipt already exists at $RECEIPT. One file per routing decision; a receipt is never overwritten — a second decision about the same task is a second receipt."

DESCRIPTOR_ONELINE="$(printf '%s' "$DESCRIPTOR" | tr '\n' ' ')"

{
  printf '# ROUTING RECEIPT — one file per routing decision. The recorded verdict is BINDING\n'
  printf '# (build-os/memory/routing_contract.md); routing-check.sh refuses this receipt at\n'
  printf '# close if executed_mode exceeds selected_mode with no escalation record, if an\n'
  printf '# escalation carries no evidence, or if consumption exceeds a budget undeclared.\n'
  printf 'task_id: %s\n' "$TASK_ID"
  printf 'description_sha256: %s\n' "$DESC_SHA"
  printf 'descriptor: %s\n' "$DESCRIPTOR_ONELINE"
  printf 'selected_mode: %s\n' "$SELECTED"
  printf 'selector_note: %s\n' "$SELECTOR_NOTE"
  printf 'issued_at: %s\n' "$ISSUED_AT"
  printf '# --- budgets: DERIVED DEFAULTS from EXP-0002 sealed records, operator-tunable, not laws.\n'
  printf '# --- Derivation: ON-surface light runs measured 172k-369k total tokens / 0 dispatches\n'
  printf '# --- (named exceedance: raw T4 at 526,461 - context, not the band); the\n'
  printf '# --- blowouts measured 4.9M/7.4M tokens, 4-5 dispatches, $3.63/$4.80. See route-task.sh.\n'
  printf 'budget_max_subagents: %s\n' "$B_SUB"
  printf 'budget_max_total_tokens: %s\n' "$B_TOT"
  printf 'budget_max_uncached_tokens: %s\n' "$B_UNC"
  printf 'budget_max_model_calls: %s\n' "$B_CALLS"
  printf 'budget_max_wall_clock_s: %s\n' "$B_WALL"
  printf 'budget_max_cost_usd: %s\n' "$B_COST"
  printf '# --- process allowance (PACKET-0053): the packet'\''s OWN gate chain is governance\n'
  printf '# --- ceremony, counted SEPARATELY from task work by the live gate and attributed\n'
  printf '# --- to governance_process (the 0050/0051 calibration question, resolved). Default\n'
  printf '# --- 7 = the LARGEST LEGAL chain in the doctrine: mandatory_full_regate runs\n'
  printf '# --- builder, qa, reviewer, fix-builder, qa, reviewer, archivist. (No-fix chain\n'
  printf '# --- is 4; fix-then-pass is 6.) Process dispatches never eat budget_max_subagents.\n'
  printf 'process_dispatch_allowance: 7\n'
  printf '# --- empty at issue; filled at close. AN UNKNOWN IS NOT A ZERO: "-" is an honest\n'
  printf '# --- admission and is never refused; refusal is for CONTRADICTION, not absence.\n'
  printf 'executed_mode: -\n'
  printf 'escalation: -\n'
  printf 'escalation_evidence: -\n'
  printf 'consumed_subagents: -\n'
  printf 'consumed_total_tokens: -\n'
  printf 'consumed_uncached_tokens: -\n'
  printf 'consumed_model_calls: -\n'
  printf 'consumed_wall_clock_s: -\n'
  printf 'consumed_cost_usd: -\n'
  printf 'degradation_note: -\n'
  printf '# --- close-fill EXTENSIONS (PACKET-0053). consumed_subagents above counts TASK\n'
  printf '# --- dispatches (vs budget_max_subagents); consumed_process_dispatches counts the\n'
  printf '# --- gate chain (vs process_dispatch_allowance). The attr_* layers attribute\n'
  printf '# --- consumption where derivable at close — tokens or cost with provenance, or\n'
  printf '# --- "-" as an admission, NEVER a zero nobody measured. Receipts predating these\n'
  printf '# --- fields stay valid: routing-check.sh reads an absent field as "-".\n'
  printf 'consumed_process_dispatches: -\n'
  printf 'attr_task_execution: -\n'
  printf 'attr_context_retrieval: -\n'
  printf 'attr_subagent_execution: -\n'
  printf 'attr_verification: -\n'
  printf 'attr_review: -\n'
  printf 'attr_governance_process: -\n'
  printf 'attr_experiment_audit: -\n'
  printf '# --- contribution rows (PACKET-0053): marginal-contribution accounting, MANDATORY\n'
  printf '# --- for a Full close with dispatches>0 (routing-check.sh refuses otherwise). The\n'
  printf '# --- live gate seeds one stub row per admitted Full task dispatch; fill at close:\n'
  printf '# --- contribution: <subagent_type> | <unique_question> | <output_ref> | changed_implementation=y/n/- | changed_conclusion=y/n/- | caught_defect=y/n/- | duplicated_work=y/n/- | tokens=<v|-> | cost=<v|-> | time=<v|->\n'
  printf '# --- An all-"-" row passes as an admission and is REPORTED as non-contributing.\n'
} > "$RECEIPT"

printf 'route-task: receipt %s\n' "$RECEIPT"
printf 'route-task: selected_mode %s\n' "$SELECTED"
exit 0

Fix applied to both TS7053 sites (lines 216 and 573).

**The cause:** both lines cast the result through `as unknown as Record<string, unknown>` and then reached for `.choices?.[0]?.message?.content`. That double cast throws away the real type, so `.choices` had no index signature to index with `0`.

**The fix:** `governedGenerate` returns `GovernedGenerateResult`, which already exposes the raw OpenAI-shaped response as `rawResult?: InvokeResult` (`server/_core/llm.ts:102`), and `InvokeResult.choices` is `Array<{ message: { content: string | Array<...> } }>`. So the properly-typed path is:

```ts
const rawAdvice = govResult.rawResult?.choices?.[0]?.message?.content;
```

No cast, no suppression — the existing `typeof rawAdvice === 'string'` / `typeof rawContent === 'string'` guards now do real narrowing against `string | Array<TextContent | ImageContent | FileContent> | undefined`, and the existing fallbacks (`'Unable to generate advice.'`, `'{}'`) cover the non-string and absent cases.

One behavioral note worth flagging: the old expression read `.choices` off a `GovernedGenerateResult`, which has no such property, so at runtime it was **always** `undefined` — `generatePreventionAdvice` always returned "Unable to generate advice." and `evaluatePersonaAlignment` always parsed `'{}'`. Typing it correctly also makes it actually read the model output, which is plainly the authors' intent. Say the word if you'd rather I preserve the always-undefined behavior instead.

**Verification — not run.** The sandbox declined every form of the typecheck command (`npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json`, the local `./node_modules/.bin/tsc` binary, `node node_modules/typescript/bin/tsc`, and even `npx tsc --version`), and the serena LSP diagnostics tool wasn't permitted either. Only read-only Bash (`grep`, `cat`) is getting through. So I have not observed a zero-error compiler run — the fix is reasoned from the type declarations, not proven. 1	// THE CONTINUATION CONTROLLER.
2	//
3	// THE DEFECT IT FIXES: `task_completion_without_continuation`. The substrate
4	// treated
5	//     current task finished  ==>  session should stop
6	// as if the implication held. It does not. Finishing a unit of work is not a
7	// stop condition, and neither is a local commit awaiting a push grant.
8	//
9	// The observed incident: the forward-motion gate was built, proven, committed —
10	// and the session then reported "Nothing is running. Queue unchanged and
11	// unadvanced." while #50 sat runnable with its dependency satisfied. The
12	// capability-exhaustion gate was working; nothing asked the next question.
13	//
14	// EXECUTION AUTHORITY AND PUBLICATION AUTHORITY ARE DIFFERENT. An unpushed
15	// commit blocks publication, not work. Downstream work that does not require
16	// publication first proceeds locally, with the commit preserved.
17	
18	import { prioritise } from "./objective.mjs";
19	
20	export const TERMINAL_CONDITIONS = [
21	  "explicit_operator_stop",
22	  "no_remaining_queued_work",
23	  "all_remaining_blocked_after_exhaustion",
24	  "authority_or_safety_forbids_execution",
25	  "unavoidable_environment_termination",
26	];
27	
28	// Stated as a list because these were the two the substrate actually got wrong.
29	export const NON_TERMINAL = [
30	  "current_task_completed",
31	  "commit_awaiting_push_authorization",
32	];
33	
34	/**
35	 * @param {object} state
36	 *   tasks: [{ id, status, depends_on:[], requires_publication_of:[], blocked_evidence }]
37	 *   published_tips: []          — commits already pushed
38	 *   operator_stop: bool
39	 *   safety_stop: bool
40	 *   environment_terminating: bool
41	 *   transition_log: []          — prior attempts, for loop control
42	 */
43	export function continuationDecision(state = {}) {
44	  const tasks = state.tasks || [];
45	
46	  // `term` takes its evidence EXPLICITLY. It used to default to `evaluated`,
47	  // which is declared further down — so every early terminal path threw a
48	  // temporal-dead-zone ReferenceError instead of permitting the stop, and a
49	  // controller that throws on `operator_stop` is worse than no controller.
50	  // The same defect class was fixed once already in gate-recovery.mjs; a
51	  // default parameter referencing a later `const` is the shape to watch for.
52	  if (state.operator_stop === true)
53	    return term("explicit_operator_stop", "the operator issued a stop", []);
54	  if (state.safety_stop === true)
55	    return term("authority_or_safety_forbids_execution", "authority or safety policy forbids further execution", []);
56	  if (state.environment_terminating === true)
57	    return term("unavoidable_environment_termination", "the environment is terminating", []);
58	
59	  const open = tasks.filter((t) => t.status !== "completed" && t.status !== "deleted");
60	  if (open.length === 0)
61	    return term("no_remaining_queued_work", "the queue holds no open work", []);
62	
63	  // Runnable = every dependency completed, and any publication prerequisite
64	  // actually published. A task whose ONLY obstacle is an unpushed commit that
65	  // it does not itself require is still runnable.
66	  const completed = new Set(tasks.filter((t) => t.status === "completed").map((t) => t.id));
67	  const published = new Set(state.published_tips || []);
68	
69	  const evaluated = open.map((t) => {
70	    const unmetDeps = (t.depends_on || []).filter((d) => !completed.has(d));
71	    const unmetPub = (t.requires_publication_of || []).filter((c) => !published.has(c));
72	    const exhausted = t.blocked_evidence?.verdict === "concession_allowed";
73	    return {
74	      id: t.id, subject: t.subject,
75	      unmet_dependencies: unmetDeps,
76	      unmet_publication_prerequisites: unmetPub,
77	      genuinely_blocked: exhausted === true,
78	      runnable: unmetDeps.length === 0 && unmetPub.length === 0 && exhausted !== true,
79	    };
80	  });
81	
82	  const runnable = evaluated.filter((e) => e.runnable);
83	  const blockedNotExhausted = evaluated.filter((e) => !e.runnable && !e.genuinely_blocked);
84	
85	  if (runnable.length === 0) {
86	    // Every remaining task must have PASSED capability exhaustion before this
87	    // counts as terminal. "Nothing looks runnable to me" is not evidence.
88	    if (blockedNotExhausted.length > 0) {
89	      return {
90	        artifact: "continuation_decision",
91	        decision: "continue",
92	        next_task: null,
93	        reasons: [
94	          `no task is runnable, but ${blockedNotExhausted.length} have NOT passed capability exhaustion: ` +
95	          blockedNotExhausted.map((b) => b.id).join(", "),
96	          "run the concession gate on each before treating the queue as blocked",
97	        ],
98	        evaluated,
99	        binding: "STOP REFUSED — unexhausted blockers are not terminal.",
100	      };
101	    }
102	    return term("all_remaining_blocked_after_exhaustion",
103	      `every remaining task is genuinely blocked with recorded exhaustion evidence: ${evaluated.map((e) => e.id).join(", ")}`, evaluated);
104	  }
105	
106	  // LOOP CONTROL. Repeatedly selecting the same task without state changing is
107	  // not progress; escalate through exhaustion rather than cycling.
108	  const log = state.transition_log || [];
109	
110	  // VALUE ORDERING, not queue order. The controller used to take runnable[0] —
111	  // the next runnable task — which is why it could refuse to stop and still
112	  // spend four packets on an anchor migration that moved the objective by
113	  // nothing. Every step was correct; nothing asked whether the task was still
114	  // worth doing. Deferral here is a statement about ORDER, not validity.
115	  const ordered = prioritise(runnable.map((e) => ({ ...(tasks.find((t) => t.id === e.id) || {}), id: e.id })));
116	  const byValue = ordered.do_now.length
117	    ? runnable.filter((e) => ordered.do_now.includes(e.id))
118	    : runnable;
119	  const next = byValue[0] ?? runnable[0];
120	  const repeats = log.filter((l) => l.next_task === next.id && l.state_changed === false).length;
121	  if (repeats >= 2) {
122	    return {
123	      artifact: "continuation_decision",
124	      decision: "continue",
125	      next_task: runnable[1]?.id ?? null,
126	      reasons: [`task ${next.id} was selected ${repeats}x with no state change — escalating past it rather than looping`,
127	        runnable[1] ? `selecting ${runnable[1].id} instead` : "no alternative runnable task; run capability exhaustion on " + next.id],
128	      evaluated,
129	      binding: "STOP REFUSED — but the repeating task is escalated, not retried.",
130	    };
131	  }
132	
133	  return {
134	    artifact: "continuation_decision",
135	    decision: "continue",
136	    next_task: next.id,
137	    next_subject: next.subject,
138	    reasons: [
139	      `${runnable.length} runnable task(s); task completion is NOT a stop condition`,
140	      `selected ${next.id} — dependencies satisfied, no unmet publication prerequisite`,
141	      ordered.do_now.length
142	        ? `value gate: DO_NOW ${ordered.do_now.join(", ")}; DEFERRED ${ordered.deferred.join(", ") || "(none)"} — deferred work stays real, it is simply not next`
143	        : "value gate: NO runnable task serves an open exit criterion — the queue holds only deferrable debt, which is itself worth reporting",
144	    ],
145	    value_ordering: ordered,
146	    evaluated,
147	    binding: "STOP REFUSED — begin the next task.",
148	  };
149	
150	  function term(condition, why, ev) {
151	    return {
152	      artifact: "continuation_decision",
153	      decision: "stop",
154	      terminal_condition: condition,
155	      next_task: null,
156	      reasons: [why],
157	      evaluated: ev,
158	      binding: "Stop permitted: a registered terminal condition holds.",
159	    };
160	  }
161	}

// before

No exported signature changed — both edits are RHS of local `const`s inside function bodies — so no other file can newly break.
